e.etymology: A modern American name in the family of Jalen, Kaylen and Braylen, built on Day- or Dale with the popular -len ending.
A respelling of River, the English word, which comes from Old French riviere and Latin ripa, riverbank. River became a first name in the late 20th century.
A modern Indian name that joins the names of the Hindu gods Krishna and Shiva.
A spelling of Jensen, the Danish surname meaning son of Jens, the Danish form of John. In England Jenson also arose separately as son of Jen or Jan, medieval short forms of John.
namesakes: Jenson Button (British Formula One world champion)

e.etymology: A modern American name in the family of Amaya, Amia and Amya, written with the -iah ending of names like Mariah and Aaliyah.
A feminine respelling of Mason, the English occupational surname for a stoneworker, from Old French masson. The spelling borrows the look of Maisie and the -syn ending.
A respelling of the English word blessing, a gift of divine favor, written the way it is often said and finished with the fashionable -yn ending.
A recent Indian name used by Hindu families, part of the wave of Aa- names such as Aarav and Aarush.
From Arabic Khadija, traditionally explained as early-born or premature child. Khadijah was the first wife of the Prophet Muhammad and the first person to accept Islam.
namesakes: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid (first wife of the Prophet Muhammad)
Khadijah James (Queen Latifah's character on Living Single)

e.etymology: From Italian violetta, violet, or a pet form of the older name Viola. Verdi gave it to Violetta Valery, the heroine of his 1853 opera La traviata.
namesakes: Violetta Valery (heroine of Verdi's opera La traviata)

e.meaning: short for Lincoln, settlement by the pool
e.etymology: A short form of Lincoln, the English city whose Roman name Lindum Colonia joins a Celtic word for pool with Latin colonia, settlement. Lincoln became an American first name in honor of Abraham Lincoln.
namesakes: Link (hero of Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda games)
Link Larkin (teen idol in the musical Hairspray)

assoc.t: Link, hero of Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda games
link, the everyday word for a connection or hyperlink

e.note: Gamers will think of Link from The Legend of Zelda at once; it is also an everyday word.

e.etymology: The Latin form of Greek melaina, dark or black. Two Roman saints, Melania the Elder and her granddaughter Melania the Younger, carried it, and it is the source of Melanie.
namesakes: Melania Trump (First Lady of the United States)
e.note: Closely tied to First Lady Melania Trump, so some people will read politics into the choice.

e.etymology: An English and Scottish surname from Middle English stele, steel, given either to a metal worker or to someone thought as hard as steel. Its use as a first name is recent.
A modern combination of Rose and Lynn that doubles as a spelling of Rosalyn, a name going back to the medieval Rosalind.
The Arabic form of Ishmael, from Hebrew Yishma'el, God hears. In the Bible and the Quran Ishmael is the elder son of Abraham, honored in Islam as a prophet and an ancestor of the Arabs.
The French feminine of Denis, from Latin Dionysia, a follower of Dionysus, the Greek god of wine. It was one of the most popular American girls' names of the 1950s and 1960s.
namesakes: Denise Huxtable (Lisa Bonet's character on The Cosby Show)

e.etymology: A minor Biblical name: Jeriah was a Levite chief in 1 Chronicles. Scholars read the Hebrew differently, as God sees or taught by God. In the US it also fits the sound of Jeremiah and Josiah.
From the Hawaiian word makoa, brave or fearless, related to koa, which means both warrior and the native koa tree.
In Greek myth Eris is the goddess of strife, and her name is the Greek word for it. Albanian families use Eris for boys, from a word for wind. A dwarf planet was named Eris in 2006.

assoc.t: Eris, Greek goddess of strife and discord

e.note: Eris is the Greek goddess of discord, whose golden apple started the quarrel behind the Trojan War.

e.etymology: A modern American name that puts an A- in front of Nyla, in the style of Anaya and Aniyah.
An Italian double name fused into one: Gian, short for Giovanni (John), plus Carlo (Charles). It matches French Jean-Charles and Spanish Juan Carlos.
The Scandinavian, German and Dutch spelling of Sophie, from Greek sophia, wisdom. The name spread through the early martyr Saint Sophia and many European royals.
A K- spelling of Callen or Callan, surnames of Irish and Scottish origin, in step with Kellen and Kaden.
The Greek form of Aset, the Egyptian goddess of motherhood and magic, wife of Osiris and mother of Horus. Her Egyptian name is written with the throne sign and is usually read as throne.

assoc.t: ISIS, acronym of the Islamic State terrorist group
Isis, Egyptian goddess of motherhood and magic

e.note: Since 2014 the name reads like ISIS, the Islamic State terror group, and its US use dropped sharply.

e.etymology: A single-n spelling of Giovanni, the Italian form of John, from Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious. This spelling is favored in Latin American families.

e.meaning: red-haired; also a reddish horse coat
e.etymology: Used as a trim form of Rowan, from Irish Ruadhán, little red-haired one. Roan is also the English word for a horse's coat of red mixed with white, and a boys' name in the Netherlands.

assoc.t: roan, a horse coat of red mixed with white

e.etymology: A Persian and Arabic form of Elijah, from Arabic Ilyas and Hebrew Eliyahu, my God is Yahweh. The prophet Elijah is honored in Judaism, Christianity and Islam.
A K- spelling of Camille, the French form of Latin Camilla. In Rome a camillus or camilla was a noble youth who assisted at religious rites. Kamille is also the German and Danish word for chamomile.
From Arabic rahim, merciful. Ar-Rahim, the Merciful, is one of the names of God in Islam, and Raheem can be short for Abdur Rahim, servant of the Merciful.
namesakes: Radio Raheem (boombox-carrying character in Do the Right Thing)

e.etymology: A modern spelling of Delaney, an Irish surname, that also picks up the -lani ending of Hawaiian names such as Leilani.
Lowen is the Cornish word for joyful, as in Nadelik Lowen, Merry Christmas. In the US it took off after Colleen Hoover's thriller Verity, whose narrator is the writer Lowen Ashleigh.
namesakes: Lowen Ashleigh (narrator of Colleen Hoover's novel Verity)

assoc.t: Lowen Ashleigh, narrator of Colleen Hoover's Verity
